'''Neil Samuel Charles Sullivan'''<ref name=thesis/> (born January 18, 1942) is a distinguished [[professor]] of [[physics]] at the [[University of Florida]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.phys.ufl.edu/faculty/sullivan.shtml |title=Neil Sullivan |website=Department of Physics Faculty |publisher=University of Florida |accessdate=22 July 2016}}</ref> He is one of the founders of the Micro Kelvin Laboratory of the University of Florida. He is known for the discovery of quadrupolar glass phase of [[solid hydrogen]].

== Early life and education ==
Born in New Zealand, Sullivan attended [[Otago University]], where he received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in physics in 1964<ref name="thesis" /> followed by a [[Master of Science]] in 1965.{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}} In 1972, he obtained his [[PhD]] from [[Harvard University]] with the thesis ''Nuclear Magnetism of Solid Hydrogen at Low Temperatures'', supervised by [[Robert Pound]].<ref name=thesis/>

He became a naturalized United States citizen in 2004.{{citation needed|date=July 2016}}

==Career==
In the 1970s, Sullivan worked in France at [[CEA Paris-Saclay|CEA Saclay]] with [[Anatole Abragam]]. During this time, he was the doctoral advisor of [[Michel Devoret]] and {{Ill|Daniel Esteve|fr}}.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Abragam |first=A. |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/De_la_physique_avant_toute_chose/WNdHAwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michel+devoret+neil+sullivan+abragam&pg=PA255&printsec=frontcover |title=De la physique avant toute chose |date=2000 |publisher=Odile Jacob |isbn=978-2-7381-9064-2 |language=fr}}</ref>

Sullivan left France became a professor of physics at the University of Florida in 1983. He became chair of the Physics Department in 1989, a position he held until 1999. It was during this time that he was one of three lead collaborators to successfully propose the creation of the [[National High Magnetic Field Laboratory]] in Tallahassee, Florida.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://nationalmaglab.org/about/history |title=National High Magnetic Field Laboratory History |accessdate=31 July 2020}}</ref> 
From 2000-2006, he served as Dean of the [[University of Florida College of Liberal Arts and Sciences|College of Liberal Arts and Sciences]]. He is also one of the [[editors-in-chief]] of the ''[[Journal of Low Temperature Physics]]''. In 2024 he was given the title "Distinguished Professor".{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}}

In 1987 he was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]], his citation reading ''"for fundamental studies of quantum solids using NMR techniques: contributions to orientational transitions in adsorbed N2 and solid hydrogen, discovery of a quadrupolar glass state in hydrogen, and elucidation of vacancies in solid 3He"'' <ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1987&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate= 24 September 2020}} </ref>
